newsitem.title: FRANCE: France takes step against commuter train bombings.
newsitem.headline: France takes step against commuter train bombings.

text.p: Two months after four people died in the bombing of a Paris underground train, French transport officials announced new steps on Friday to guard against further attacks on commuters.

Officials of the Paris transit authority and the national railways said they had begun to install devices on all RER commuter express trains in the capital area intended to prevent people from slipping bags or packages under the seats which might contain bombs.
Three commuter trains have been hit since 1995 by bombings blamed on Algerian Moslem extremists. In each case, authorities said the bombs were concealed in bags placed under commuter train seats.
The latest bombing was on December 3 at the Port Royal station in southern Paris.

Officials said the protective devices would be put in place under some 80,000 seats by the end of the year, beginning with the A and B lines of the RER system. The C and D lines of the RER would be equipped later.
Officials put the cost of the step at 15 million francs ($2.6 million) but "you cannot put a price on security," Transport Minister Bernard Pons told reporters.
